result.title: Truncate or Not? A Scaling Study of Looped Transformers with Truncated Backpropagation
result.summary: Looped transformers reuse a shared block of layers to increase computational depth without increasing the number of trainable parameters. They are trained with backpropagation through time (BPTT). To save training compute, BPTT is often truncated to the last few loops, although this may weaken the benefit of looping. To study this tradeoff systematically, we jointly vary model size, training tokens, and forward and backward loop counts across nearly 600 training runs and fit a unified scaling law that captures the effects of looping and truncation through effective parameters. Despite the training-compute savings of truncation, our fitted law favors full BPTT when forward and backward loop counts are jointly optimized. In matched-compute runs, full BPTT through fewer loops consistently outperforms truncated settings of the same compute. The law further shows that at fixed model size, the compute-optimal loop count and training-token budget both grow with compute. When model size is also free, the law identifies two fully trained loops as the best looped setting. Experimentally, this setting achieves lower loss than the compute-optimal non-looped model with about 27% fewer non-embedding parameters and only 8% more training compute.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用近600次训练实验，联合变化模型规模、训练token数与前向/反向循环次数，拟合统一缩放律，考察循环Transformer中截断BPTT的收益与代价，并比较全BPTT与截断在等计算量下的表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 循环块复用、循环次数与梯度截断的缩放关系，可能为loop式latent推理的循环深度选取、训练监督方式与计算分配提供可核查线索，尤其涉及最优循环次数随计算增长的趋势；但原文任务是语言建模损失，未涉及多模态推理状态，联系需人工判断。
